correctness.rationale: The formula e=(q^3-1)/14 gives order three modulo e and gcd(e,q-1)=t. A telescoping quotient-remainder identity shows that all fourteen positive multiples je with je<q^3 have base-q digit sums equal to t times (3,2,3,2,3,4,3,2,3,4,3,4,3,6). Any zero sum of length below 2t must have exactly t terms modulo t; reducing exponents modulo three would realize a multiple je below q^3 with digit sum t, impossible. Explicit three-digit expressions for 2e attain 2t. The unique minimal j=2,4,8 give the three rotations. The polynomial inequality e<(t+1)^3-1 holds for all t>=4. Standalone exact BFS independently checks all finite residues for twenty parameter values and all fourteen digit sums for 228 values; not treated as infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The 2022 Jacob--Külshammer preprint motivates the k=2 sharpness question but does not give this order-three two-progression equality or the three-vector rigidity. Breuer et al. Proposition 2.22 already gives the general orbit/digit-sum minimization, which can be specialized to this case by a finite calculation; no novelty is claimed for that general method or for the elementary digit identity. The new articulated conclusion is the parameter-uniform identification of the smallest even order-three quotient, equality at the cubic conjectural bound across an infinite family including prime bases, and classification of all reduced optimal triples. Actual targeted mathematical-record and public literature searches found no matching explicit uniform conclusion; priority beyond the inspected sources is not certified.
residual_risks: The uniform z=14 evaluation is an elementary specialisation of Breuer et al. Proposition 2.22; a stronger statement of the kind claimed may already be considered a routine corollary despite no explicit formulation being identified.

value.rationale: The first unproved k=2 bound in Jacob--Külshammer Conjecture 4 has an independently motivated sharpness question. Among even quotients z of q^3-1, z=14 is the smallest permitting an order-three unit. The family supplies an infinite, cubic-scale sharpness construction with e/t^3 -> 4/7, including infinitely many prime bases, and an exact count and description of optimal count vectors. This arithmetic boundary and rigidity are the motivated facts, rather than a table of unrelated small moduli. The finite fourteen-entry evaluation is simple given Breuer et al., a limitation explicitly acknowledged.
